summary: Place a carpet of length L over non-overlapping white tile intervals to cover the maximum number of white tiles.
mainInsight: Sort the intervals. The optimal carpet can start at the left end of some tile interval. Use two pointers: for each left interval i, advance j while interval j is fully covered (r_j <= start + L - 1), keeping a covered total, then add the partial overlap with interval j.

approaches.name: Sort + two pointers
approaches.summary: Start at each interval's left end, extend j.

approaches.name: Prefix sums + binary search
approaches.summary: Prefix of covered tiles, binary search the end.

commonMistakes: Starting the carpet only at integer 1

promptVariants: Where can an optimal carpet start?
Which starts do you need to try?
options: At the left end of a tile interval
At any integer position between the first and last tile
At the centre of the longest interval
At the right end of the final interval
cards.answer: At the left end of a tile interval
cards.explanation: Moving the carpet left until it touches a white tile never reduces the cover.

incorrectOptionExplanations.At any integer position between the firs: That range can be huge; only interval starts matter.
incorrectOptionExplanations.At the centre of the longest interval: A shorter interval may give a better cover.
incorrectOptionExplanations.At the right end of the final interval: That only covers the last tile run.

promptVariants: How do you count the partial overlap with the next interval?
What is the formula for the last, partially covered interval?
cards.answer: With the carpet ending at end = start + L - 1, after fully covered intervals the next interval j contributes max(0, end - l_j + 1) tiles (its start up to the carpet end). The sum of full intervals plus this partial piece is the cover for that start.
cards.explanation: Both pointers only move forward, so the total work is linear after sorting.
Sorting dominates; the pointer sweep is linear.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Space complexity (excluding the input): ___
What is the answer when the carpet is longer than all tiles combined?
options: All tiles: the carpet can start at the first interval and cover every one
Only the longest single interval can ever be covered
Zero: the carpet must match a tile run exactly
The carpet length, counting the gaps as white tiles too
cards.answer: All tiles: the carpet can start at the first interval and cover every one
cards.explanation: The cover is the total white tile count.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Only the longest single interval can eve: A long carpet can cover them all.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Zero: the carpet must match a tile run e: A carpet may overlap many intervals.

canonicalCode:
class Solution:
    def maximumWhiteTiles(self, tiles: List[List[int]], carpetLen: int) -> int:
        tiles.sort()
        best = covered = j = 0
        for i, (l, r) in enumerate(tiles):         # carpet starts at the left end of tile i
            end = l + carpetLen - 1
            while j < len(tiles) and tiles[j][1] <= end:
                covered += tiles[j][1] - tiles[j][0] + 1   # interval j fully covered
                j += 1
            partial = 0
            if j < len(tiles) and tiles[j][0] <= end:
                partial = end - tiles[j][0] + 1            # part of interval j
            best = max(best, covered + partial)
            if j == i:                                     # nothing left to drop
                j += 1
            else:
                covered -= r - l + 1                       # drop interval i before moving on
        return best
